title: What the zone report costs
prompt: Before the trips-per-pickup-zone report goes on the nightly schedule, the platform team wants to know how much work it is. Write `solve(trips)` so it returns the trips per pickup zone, with the number of stages and tasks that one `collect()` of those counts runs.
rules: Count the trips per `pickup_zone_id` with `groupBy(...).count()`. Trips with no pickup zone form a group of their own.
Measure with adaptive execution off: set `spark.sql.adaptive.enabled` to `"false"` first, so the job follows the plan.
`stages` is the number of stages in the job that `collect()` starts; `tasks` is the total number of tasks across those stages.
Return the columns `pickup_zone_id`, `count`, `stages`, `tasks`; `with_counts` in the starter adds the last two.
hints: Start a fresh group with `name = new_job_group("zones")`, call `collect()`, then read the job with `tracker.getJobIdsForGroup(name)`.
`getJobInfo(job).stageIds` lists the job's stages and `getStageInfo(stage).numTasks` gives each one's tasks. Add those up for `tasks`.
A grouping job has one stage more than its plan has `Exchange` steps. Measure the `collect()` itself: a `count()` on the grouped DataFrame is a different job.
explanation: With adaptive execution off, `collect()` on the grouped DataFrame is one job with two stages: 1 task reads the one-file table and counts within it, then the shuffle makes 4 partitions (this environment's `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions`), so 4 tasks add up the counts. That's 2 stages and 5 tasks, on every input here, because the input is always one small file. You can measure it with `statusTracker()` or work it out from the plan: one `Exchange`, so two stages; `trips.rdd.getNumPartitions()` plus `by_zone.rdd.getNumPartitions()` tasks. The usual slips: leaving adaptive execution on (Spark then runs the first stage as a job of its own), counting only the last stage's tasks, or measuring `by_zone.count()`, which adds a third stage to total the groups.
